diagnoses.description: Intervertebral disc disorders with radiculopathy, lumbosacral region
Other symptoms and signs involving the musculoskeletal system (left plantarflexion weakness)

claim.clinicalNotes:
DATE OF VISIT: 2026-09-15. Follow-up, spine clinic.
HPI: 47-year-old male with low back pain radiating down the posterior left leg to the lateral foot since 2026-07-14 (9 weeks). Pain 7/10, worse with sitting and coughing. Reports numbness of the lateral left foot and difficulty pushing off with the left foot when walking.
CONSERVATIVE TREATMENT: Completed 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy (12 sessions, 2026-07-21 to 2026-08-29) with McKenzie extension program and core stabilization, without improvement. Naproxen 500 mg twice daily for 8 weeks and a methylprednisolone dose pack on 2026-08-04 with only transient relief. Activity modification and home exercise program ongoing.
EXAM: Positive straight leg raise on the left at 35 degrees reproducing radicular pain below the knee. Left ankle (Achilles) reflex absent; right 2+. Left plantarflexion strength 4/5; unable to perform single-leg heel raise on the left. Decreased light-touch sensation over the lateral left foot (S1 dermatome). Gait antalgic.
RED FLAGS: No bowel or bladder dysfunction, no saddle anesthesia, no fever, no weight loss, no history of cancer.
IMAGING: Lumbar spine X-rays 2026-07-21: mild L5-S1 disc space narrowing, no fracture or listhesis. No prior lumbar MRI.
ASSESSMENT: Left S1 radiculopathy with objective neurological deficit (absent Achilles reflex, plantarflexion weakness), persisting after more than 6 weeks of conservative therapy. Suspect L5-S1 disc herniation.
PLAN: MRI lumbar spine without contrast to define the lesion and plan treatment; the patient is a candidate for an epidural steroid injection or surgical consultation depending on findings.
